customData.page_goal: Get homeowners in north Spokane and on Five Mile Prairie to ask for an on-site tree removal quote by phone or through the form.
customData.site_description: Lead-generation site for tree removal in Spokane. Calls and quote requests go to the local tree crew that rents the site. Most callers are homeowners with a tall pine or a dead tree close to the house, garage or fence.

customData.included_services:
Removal of whole trees, including tall pines close to a house, garage or fence
Taking a tree down in sections by climbing when there is no room to fell it
Hauling away branches and trunk wood
Stump grinding, quoted separately as an add-on
Cutting trunk wood into rounds and leaving it on site when the homeowner wants to keep it
customData.excluded_services:
Trimming or pruning trees that stay
Any tree in contact with power lines
Filling the stump hole with topsoil or seed
Splitting firewood
customData.business_facts:
Quotes are free and given after the crew looks at the tree in person
The homeowner does not need to be home for the quote if the tree can be seen from the street or the yard is open
Branches and trunk wood are hauled away unless the homeowner asks to keep the wood
Calls and quote forms are answered on business days
Phone: (509) 555-0142 (calls and texts)
customData.local_notes:
Some lots have tall pines growing close to the house, garage or fence (written by us for this test)
Some lots are reached from an alley, with narrow side yards; when the gate is too narrow for equipment, the crew carries branches and wood out by hand (written by us for this test)
City of Spokane: a tree on private property needs no city permit; any removal of a tree in the public right-of-way needs an Urban Forestry permit, and the right-of-way width varies from street to street, so check before working on trees near roads or alleys; unsure: Urban Forestry, 509.363.5495 (source: https://my.spokanecity.org/urbanforestry/permits/)
Avista customers: Avista does not prune around the service wire that runs from the pole to the house; the homeowner can request a no-cost service drop at (800) 227-9187, which de-energizes and temporarily removes the line so the homeowner or their contractor can safely do the work; available Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3 p.m., requested at least three business days in advance (source: https://www.myavista.com/safety/tree-trimming/frequently-asked-questions)
customData.cta: Call (509) 555-0142 or send the quote form to book a free on-site quote
